I am a Principal Economist at the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and previously served as an economist at the Federal Trade Commission and the Department of Justice Antitrust Division. My research focuses on antitrust and competition policy, especially merger review, market definition, and the use of economic evidence under uncertainty.

Across nearly two decades of public service, I have led economic investigations and supported high-profile litigations involving retail banking, semiconductors, health insurance, cinema and radio advertising, airlines, and parking services. Banking is an important application of this broader agenda: it has been central to U.S. merger law since *Philadelphia National Bank* and offers unusually rich public data for studying merger effects.

To support this enforcement and policy analysis, I develop open-source software—including the R packages `antitrust`, `trade`, and `competitiontoolbox`—that translates modern structural industrial organization models into practical quantitative tools.
